brief: Calculate a vehicle’s total ownership cost including maintenance, insurance and depreciation assumptions.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Vehicle Costs"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "El costo de un vehículo"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "O custo de um veículo"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Calculate a vehicle’s total ownership cost including maintenance, insurance and depreciation assumptions.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A low vehicle price can hide high running costs; compare fictional dollars for the whole ownership period.
instruction.misconception: Vehicle cost equals sticker price or fuel alone, and value lost at resale does not count.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Compare purchase minus resale value, plus stated running and financing costs. Do not count the purchase price twice.
Value lost equals purchase price minus resale value.
Operating the vehicle involves more than fuel.
Add value lost to all stated costs of use.
Net value loss already accounts for purchase and resale.
Unknown repairs can change the ownership cost comparison.
Fuel savings alone do not establish the lower total cost.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.

en-US.line: A low vehicle price can hide high running costs; compare fictional dollars for the whole ownership period.

pt-BR.line: Um preço baixo pode esconder custos altos de uso; compare reais fictícios por todo o período de posse.
